title: fix(ui): orthographic depth maps into WebGPU's clip volume, not OpenGL's
body:
The ortho branch of `Camera::mvp` mapped depth the way OpenGL's `glOrtho` does - NDC z over [-1, +1]. WebGPU's clip volume wants `0 <= z <= w`, and the ortho matrix holds `clip.w == 1` (the #434 law tests pin that), so every point nearer than `(near + far) / 2` was clipped away before rasterization. With `far = 40 * dist`, that cut plane sits twenty times the orbit distance out: everything in view, so clicking **Orthographic** blanked the viewport.

Perspective carries the same OpenGL-style z row but `clip.w` is the eye distance there, which keeps clip z positive beyond ~0.2 mm - far closer than the camera can orbit - so perspective was unaffected.

## The change

The ortho z row (`viewport.rs`, the `[col][row]` proj literal) becomes

```rust
[0.0, 0.0, 1.0 / (near - far), 0.0],
[0.0, 0.0, near / (near - far), 1.0],
```

near maps to 0.0, far to 1.0, and ortho depth is now linear. The depth attachment already clears to 1.0 under `CompareFunction::Less`, so no pipeline or shader change is needed. The x/y rows already speak WebGPU and are untouched, as is the perspective branch (its z quirk costs depth precision, not geometry - out of scope here).

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `law_tests::projection_tests::the_ortho_depth_spans_zero_to_one_between_the_planes` - depth at the near plane, the far plane, and strictly between with monotonic climb. On main: "the near plane sits at -1".
- `gpu_render::orthographic_paints_the_band_perspective_does` - the stock box from `box_stock_paints_steel_over_background` under `test_cam()`, painted in both modes, with the same band bounds and a comparability check (each within 1.5x of the other). On main: 0/65536 pixels.

## Tested

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` builds clean.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 378 passed, 5 ignored.
- `--test gpu_render`: 10 passed (9 existing + the new one).
- `--test trace_composite`: 4 passed (its first run hit the known pre-existing fallback-device crash race; clean on rerun, and it only exercises the untouched perspective path).

Changelog: orthographic view no longer blanks the viewport - the parallel depth row maps into WebGPU's clip volume (#600)

Fixes #600

title: fix(ui): the setup page's lay-on-plane controls stay on screen, so a picked face is turned flat
body:
**Stacked on #593** (#555), which is on #573 (#557 + #554). It includes their commits until they merge.

## Root cause of the reopened #330
The turn itself was never broken. `pick::lay_on_plane` / `AlignPartToSetup` turn a picked tilted face onto G17/G18/G19 on main, and a new app test pins that. What was broken is what a user could reach on the Setups page. Reproduced through the real shell (1280×720, the block turned 30° about X, real viewport clicks):
1. **Edge snapping (main):** the plane row armed Edge mode (`plane_pick.rs:31`), so a click on the tilted face took an edge, `check_lay` refused it, and Apply stayed grey. **Already fixed by #573** (7d641c8b, #554: the plane row picks faces only).
2. **Controls off screen (main and the stack):** the face row was one long line. In the ~285 px properties pane, **Flip, "Face to plane level" and Apply fell past the right edge**, so clicks on them did nothing. The only Apply in reach was the Part alignment row's angle Apply, which turns about the bounds centre. That matches the report's "it only moves the model". Without a reachable Flip, the default also lays the face's outside up, with the part below the plane.

## What changed
- **Face row:** split into short lines: label + "Pick a face"; plane + Flip; "Face to plane level"; the picked face; then **Apply face** on its own line.
- **Other rows:** the three-points row (#555) and the "Axes in the plane" rows (#557) overflowed the same way and got the same treatment.
- **Not used:** `horizontal_wrapped`, which didn't work because other rows widen the pane's content.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/330-face-lay-rotate.md`.
- **Maintainer's call:** the default Flip is unchanged: unflipped means the face's outside points along +axis, so a face picked on G17 lays "outside up". Many users will expect the picked face to become the bottom, so flipping the default may be worth it.
- **Not addressed:** the Part alignment row's angle Apply turning about the bounds centre (the "shifts relative to the origin" part of the report). Follow-up or maintainer's call.

## How tested
- **New UI real-click test:** `plane_face_lay::a_clicked_tilted_face_is_turned_flat_onto_g17_not_only_moved`.
  - It clicks Pick a face → the tilted face in the viewport, asserts Flip, "Face to plane level" and Apply face are on screen, then clicks Flip → Apply face.
  - Result: face normal −Z, face at Z 0, part above. Ctrl+Z restores.
  - It fails on main (an edge is taken) and on the stack without the layout fix (the Apply click misses).
- **Structural:** `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` asserts every option of the face, points and axes rows is inside the window.
- **App:** `plane_align::a_tilted_face_is_turned_flat_onto_each_plane_with_the_part_above_it` covers G17/G18/G19 with undo. It passes on main too, which pins that the command was right.
- **Gate:** plane_align, plane_align_edges, points_align, axis_align, setup_align, winding_align, commands_undo and ui lib 385 pass. The headless-GPU test fails only on this machine. Clippy is clean.

Changelog: Setups page "Lay on a plane": Flip, "Face to plane level" and the row's own "Apply face" stay on screen in the properties pane (they ran off its edge), so a picked tilted face can be laid flat on G17/G18/G19; the three-points and axes rows get the same fix (#330)

Fixes #330

title: feat(tools): align a vendor STEP by ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems
body:
Second slice of #370 (and part of #361): auto-aligning a vendor STEP by its ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems.

## What changed
- `ToolCsysReport::align_tool_body()` extracts the tool axis (from CIP, or CSIF if CIP is absent) and calculates the tip offset (`-dot(origin, axis)`) so that the cutting reference point sits at Z = 0 in the tool frame, pointing up into the spindle along +Z.
- `ToolBodySpec::from_step_auto(&path)` reads both mesh facets and coordinate systems from a vendor STEP file, aligning it with zero manual offsets.
- `SetToolBody::from_step_auto(&world, tool_name, &path)` attaches the auto-aligned tool body as one undoable command.
- `tool_body_view::load_aligned(&path)` returns `LoadedBody` carrying the auto-alignment result or fallback reason, preserving `load` backwards compatibility.
- In the tool editor (`ToolBodyUi`), importing a STEP file with ISO 13399 coordinate systems automatically sets the axis and tip offset with the note "aligned by ISO 13399 coordinate systems"; importing a file without them or with degenerate/ambiguous coordinate systems falls back to default numeric placement ([0, 0, 1] axis, 0 offset) with a note naming why.
- Test fixture `testdata/models/tool_csys_box_iso13399.step` combining a B-rep box and ISO 13399 placements.
- `docs/decisions/370-tool-csys-align.md`.

Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## Readings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_csys`: 9/9 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_body`: 12/12 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib tool_body`: 10/10 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests
- `iso_13399_tool_csys_aligns_automatically`
- `a_file_without_tool_csys_falls_back_by_name`
- `degenerate_tool_csys_falls_back_by_name`
- `step_with_tool_coordinate_systems_aligns_automatically`
- `step_without_tool_coordinate_systems_falls_back_by_name`
- `step_with_degenerate_coordinate_systems_falls_back_by_name`
- `tool_body_view_load_aligned_handles_step_csys_and_fallback`
- `import_tool_body_from_step_auto_aligns_in_editor`
- `import_tool_body_from_step_without_csys_falls_back_by_name_in_editor`

Changelog: Tool bodies: align a vendor STEP by its ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems (#370)

Fixes #370

title: feat(post): optionally end a Tormach program in the operator's units
body:
## What changed
After the contributor's mm probe run on a 770MX (#521 / #583), PathPilot stayed in G21. LinuxCNC's `M2`/`M30` reset MDI mode, G54, G17, G90, G94, M48, G40, M5, G1 and M9, but **not the length unit** (LinuxCNC G-code reference, M-codes, "M2, M30 Program End").

A new Tormach post option, **End in**, takes one of three values:
- **Program's unit** (the default, byte-identical output);
- **Inch (G20)**;
- **mm (G21)**.

When the choice differs from the program's unit, `G20`/`G21` is written on its own line after the final `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30` and right before `M30`, so no move is read in the new unit.
- **Setting:** `PostOptions.end_units` (`EndUnits` in schema.rs), set through the existing undoable `SetPostOptions`.
- **Project file:** an optional `post_options.end_units` key; a missing key means the default, so there is no version step. An unknown word refuses the file by name.
- **Post page:** an "End in" row, shown only while Tormach PathPilot is the post.
- **Other posts:** ignore it.
- **Dropped, with reasons in `docs/decisions/596-end-native-units.md`:**
  - a machine-file `native_unit` key, which would need a guess written into every stock file;
  - a closing comment only;
  - an on/off switch.

## How tested
- **New `tormach_end_units` (7):**
  - the default writes no key, and the output is byte-identical;
  - a mm program for an inch control ends `G53 G0 Z0 / G30 / G20 / M30`, and the G20 line is the only difference;
  - an inch program for a mm control ends with G21;
  - matching units add nothing;
  - undo and redo;
  - round-trip, including the unknown-word refusal.
  - The two G20/G21 tests fail with the old .cps.
- **UI:** `after_op_tests::end_units_choice_commits_and_undoes`.
- **Gate:** tormach_post, tormach_machines, conformance (goldens unchanged), posting, program_entry, project_roundtrip, after_op, lathe_post_g76, per_op_files and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy (post/app/ui) is clean.

## Not exercised
A PathPilot Hub run with the option set.

Changelog: Tormach post: new "End in" post option (default off) writes G20/G21 before M30, so a program can leave PathPilot in the operator's units (LinuxCNC's M30 does not reset G20/G21) (#596)

Fixes #596

title: fix(app): a probe-only program's stock sim judges the uncut stock
body:
## What changed

A probe-only program posted with "stock sim did not judge this program: invalid stock simulation setup: stock box and cell must be finite, box non-empty, cell positive". That names the wrong cause; the stock was fine.

**Cause:**
- A touch probe stays out of the program sim's plan, because it removes nothing (#108). In a probe-only program the plan is therefore empty.
- The stock lattice is sized by `min(radius)` over the planned tools, which is +inf over an empty plan.
- The infinite cell was then refused as an invalid setup.

**Fix (`crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs`, `stock_grid`):** when no tool radius is finite, the lattice is sized by the stock's span alone (`auto_cell(0, span)`, the grid ceiling's floor).
- **What the sim does now:** it judges the uncut stock against the part. That reads clean when they agree and rest where they differ, and it cannot report a gouge it never cut.
- **Unchanged:** a missing or invalid stock still refuses by its own name, and `auto_cell` in the sim crate is untouched.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/592-probe-only-sim.md`. It records why I judged the uncut stock rather than skipping the sim with a note.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/probe_only_sim.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `a_probe_only_program_is_judged_not_refused_as_an_invalid_setup`: a 3 × 2 × 1 in part with stock equal to it, and one top-face probe. `verification_report` has no problems and **no not-judged note**. It **fails without the fix**, with the old note present.
  - `a_probe_only_program_without_a_stock_still_says_why`: no stock gives no "invalid setup" text, and any refusal names "no stock".
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`** ran the app suites: 1504 passed, 0 failed.
- **Named:** post_not_judged 4, stock_sim_document 9, setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8, posting 17, probe_op 11.
- **`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`:** clean.
- No golden or snapshot changed. Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## Not exercised

A GUI post of a probe-only job. The note is a post-report string, and the test reads the same `verification_report` the GUI shows.

Changelog: A probe-only program no longer posts with a misleading "stock sim did not judge: invalid stock simulation setup" note; the uncut stock is judged (#592)

Fixes #592

title: fix(post): comment text is escaped per dialect
body:
## What changed
Operation, setup and tool names were already cleaned by each post's `clean()` (#257), but the **machine name in the program header was written raw**. Five shipped machine files have parentheses in their names (`Tormach 770MX (ML)`, `Tormach PCNC 1100 (Series I/II/3)`, `Tormach PCNC 770 (Series 3)`), so their headers posted a nested comment such as `(Tormach 770MX (ML))`, which LinuxCNC/PathPilot refuses. Hand-edited machine names (#478's editor) could break any dialect the same way.
- **The six affected posts:** the header name now goes through the post's own `clean()`, with a fallback of `CAMCRAFT` if nothing is left.
- **Tormach:** `note()` also guards against LinuxCNC active comments. A text starting with `MSG`, `DEBUG`, `PRINT`, `LOG*`, `PROBEOPEN`/`PROBECLOSE`, `ABORT`, `AXIS` or `PY*` (any case, whole word) is prefixed with `- `, so a user's name never becomes an operator message or a log command.
- **Engine default:** `writeComment()` (js.rs) turns `(`, `)` and control characters into spaces.
- **Rules:**
  - `( )` dialects (Fanuc, Fanuc lathe, Haas, Mazak, Tormach; RS-274 / ISO 6983): `( ) % ;` become spaces, non-printable or non-ASCII characters become `?`, runs of spaces collapse, 40-character cap.
  - Sinumerik: `;` comments get the same `clean()`.
  - Heidenhain: already safe; it is now tested.
- **Not done:** no uppercasing, so existing goldens stay byte-identical. Parentheses become spaces rather than `[ ]`, because brackets are expression syntax on macro B and LinuxCNC.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/594-comment-escape.md`.

## How tested
- **New `comment_escape`:**
  - `hostile_names_post_well_formed_comments_in_every_mill_dialect`: machine `MSG, Mill (A); B*`, op `Op (1); debug*`, tool `EM(6);*`. Every line holds at most one balanced comment closed at the end of the line, with no `;` and ASCII only. Tormach writes no active comment, and the Sinumerik and Heidenhain block rules hold.
  - `hostile_names_post_well_formed_comments_on_the_lathe`.
  - `every_bundled_machine_name_posts_a_single_header_comment`: every shipped Tormach .mch.
  - All three failed before the change.
- **Gate:** the 25 post-related app suites (conformance, golden_cl, posting, and every post, lathe, inverted, coolant and comment suite) and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy is clean. **No golden changed.**

Changelog: Posts clean the machine name in the program header like every other comment (no nested "(...)" from names such as "Tormach 770MX (ML)"), and the Tormach post never writes a user name as a LinuxCNC active comment (MSG/DEBUG/PRINT/LOG...) (#594)

Fixes #594

title: feat(app): moving a part warns when it or its stock would sink into a fixture
body:
**Stacked on #576** (#571), which is on #566 (#561). It includes their commits until they merge.

## What changed
Locate (#561) already warns when the part or its stock would sink into a fixture. A plain Model-page move or turn didn't check at all (#582).
- **Shared check:** locate's sampled test and its by-name part and stock messages moved into a new `fixture_clash.rs`. `fixture_locate` calls it, and its wording is unchanged.
- **`MoveModel::new` now carries a `warning()`:**
  - the moved part is checked against every fixture in every setup, read through each setup's alignment;
  - a stock that follows the move is checked only in the setup that owns it;
  - setups with no fixtures are skipped without reading any geometry.
- **No double check in locate:** `MoveModel::locating` and the new `MoveFixture::locating` skip it, because locate runs its own check.
- **Fixture moves warn too:** `MoveFixture::new` checks the moved fixture against the setup's parts and stock.
- **Where it shows:** the status line reads `moved X - warning: …` (a shared `with_warning`), and MCP `move_fixture` gains a `"warning"` field.
- **A warning, not a refusal.** It warns on the result, so a part already inside a closed vise warns on every nudge.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/582-move-interpenetration.md`.

## How tested
- **New `move_interpenetration` (7):**
  - sinking into the floor warns by name;
  - a turn swinging into the jaw warns;
  - a stock-only sink warns for the stock alone;
  - a clear move warns nothing;
  - no fixtures means no check;
  - undo and redo of a warned move;
  - moving the fixture into the part warns.
- **UI:** `a_model_page_move_into_the_fixture_warns_on_the_status_line`.
- **Gate:** move_model_stock, commands_undo, fixture_locate(_stock), fixtures, fixture_ux, setup_align, project_roundtrip, mcp_setup and the ui fixture_ux/locate tests pass. Clippy is clean.

Changelog: A Model-page move or turn (and a Fixtures-page fixture move) warns by name when the part or its stock would sink into a fixture, as locate does - a warning, not a refusal (#582)

Fixes #582

title: refactor(sim): law (d)'s prior readers read the stock through Columns
body:
## What changed

M7.3 step 2/6 (#26 umbrella, split in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/26#issuecomment-6754685656).

Law (d)'s prior-stock readers, `verify::prior_surface` and `verify::acquit_by_prior`, took `&Dexel`, which names the column engine directly. They now take `&Columns<'_>`, the M7.3 column seam that a column or field `Stock` already answers through.

- **`Columns` gains `Columns::of_grid(&Dexel)`:** a borrowed bare rest grid, read through the same seam. The reader's source becomes an internal `Source::{Grid, Field}`, so a reader no longer needs a whole `Stock`.
- **`Columns` gains `cell()`, `center(ix, iy)` and `origin()`.**
- **The operation layer** (`drill_prior::PriorRead::surface`, `generate.rs`'s acquittal) still holds the program-ahead grid as a `Dexel`, so it wraps it with `of_grid`. #586 moves that holder onto `Stock`, and the call then becomes `stock.columns()?`.
- **Scope corrected from the research:** `solid_rest` names no `Dexel`. `carry::Body` uses `Dexel` as storage, not as a reader, so that move goes with #586/#589. It's recorded on #585 and in `docs/decisions/585-prior-readers-on-columns.md`.

The change is behaviour-neutral: `Columns` maps a point to its column by the column engine's own formula, so a grid read through it answers identically.

## How tested

- **The existing `verify::prior` unit tests pass unchanged, 4/4**, wrapped in `Columns::of_grid`.
- **New `crates/sim/tests/prior_columns.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `the_prior_surface_reads_alike_through_a_grid_and_a_field`: inside the hole, across its rim and on the raw top, the column and field stocks agree within 1e-6. It reads the hole floor at 15 and the raw top at 25.
  - `a_dive_is_acquitted_alike_on_either_engine_and_through_a_bare_grid`: a column stock, a field stock and a bare grid acquit the same dive and keep the same conviction.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`** escalated to batch. geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app all pass, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on every crate. The only reds are the 3 headless-GPU ui tests, which are environmental on this host.
- **Named:** drill_prior 12, drill_reach 6, carried_verify 8, setup_carry 9, stock_columns 3.
- No golden or snapshot changed. Branched from v0.16.0, which the fork's main is synced to.

## Not exercised

Nothing user-visible changes, so there is no GUI or machine check.

Changelog: none (internal refactor, behaviour-neutral)

Fixes #585
Refs #26

title: fix(units): status lines, refusals and the gate's gouge clause speak the document's units
body:
## What changed

Tier 1 of the #578 split (tiers and drops kept in `docs/decisions/578-units-in-errors.md`): transient strings - the ones that quote the numbers the user is already reading on screen - format at print time through `app::units::of(world)` and the pure `geometry::units` formatters. Millimeter strings stay byte-identical (the `len`/`feed`/`area` law: inches ride the mm precision plus extra decimals); only inch documents hear anything new.

- `geometry::units`: new `vol` formatter (inches get `mm_prec + 3`, mirroring `area`) and `Unit::vol_suffix`'s superscript spellings "mm³"/"in³" (matching `area_suffix`; a plain "mm3" would have changed the mm strings). Re-exported by `app::units`.
- The posting gate's gouge clause (`posting_sim::sim_clause`): worst depth and its location lens - `worst 0.1969 in at (-0.0246, -0.0738, z 0.1969)`.
- `commands/set_stock` refusal: `stock dimensions exceed 1000000 mm` - the shape changes from the old `{:e}`'s "1e6 mm" (see the correction comment on #578; the issue body's "2000 mm" misquoted it).
- `commands/cutting_data` "already runs the suggestion": spindle and feed through `feed`/`feed_suffix`.
- UI status strings: the applied-suggestion note, the tool-body tip offset, the feeds page's fz note, and the setup stock page's box range and volume (the only volume sentence in the UI).
- `ui::actions::deviate_readout` takes a `Unit` parameter, mirroring its sibling `sim_readout(&sc, t, Unit)`; both callers pass the world lens.

Held back, with reasons in the decision file: persisted notes (they freeze the unit into the `.camproj`; they want `Warning`-shaped structured notes - its own issue), machine-limit strings (those speak the machine's numbers; the inch-`.mch` unit-never-converted bug is noted on the issue, not fixed here), and the generator/pure-crate refusals (no world or unit in scope below the app).

## Pinning tests

- `blind_floor::the_gouge_clause_speaks_the_document_s_units` - the same gouging world told in inches ("... in at (...)", no "mm" anywhere); flip the lens back to mm and the sentence is unchanged.
- `egui_app::tests::deviate_readout_rides_the_units_lens` - REST and GOUGE sentences pinned in inches; the mm pins next to them untouched.

## Quick gate, green at 7775c1ff

`cargo test -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` clean, zero warnings. Then: `geometry --lib` 39, `app --lib` 101, `ui --lib` 378 (5 ignored), and the touched integration binaries `blind_floor` 7, `post_not_judged` 6, `cutting_data` 5, `edge_break_gate` 4, `commands_undo` 32, `dirty_flag` 2, `project_roundtrip` 69 - all pass.

Not exercised: the full suite (the pre-existing wgpu race upstream), and the on-screen widgets themselves - their formatting functions are pinned instead.

Changelog: errors, warnings and status notes ride the document's units - an inch document hears inches (saved notes and machine-limit messages stay mm, each its own issue).

title: feat(post): probe programs report the measured deviation on the control
body:
**Stacked on #521** (#362, Tormach PathPilot probing), which adds Tormach's probe result block. It includes #521's commits until that PR merges. #521 itself is unchanged.

## What changed
A probe program reported nothing about what it measured: on success it silently wrote `G10 L20`, and the offset table was the only trace. This came up in #521's run on a real 770MX.
- **Tormach PathPilot / LinuxCNC** (`tormach.cps` `onProbeResult`): writes `(DEBUG, PROBE <axis> ERROR #19n)` once per probed axis.
  - It sits after that axis's tolerance check, so the value shown has passed it, and before the `G10 L20`.
  - In a measure-only op it comes before its `(MSG, …)` / `M0`.
  - DEBUG shows in the status display without stopping and replaces `#n` with its value (LinuxCNC G-code reference, Messages/Comments, cited in the .cps).
- **Fanuc / Haas / Mazak:** no report. Custom macro B has only `#3000` (alarm) and `#3006` (stop with message), and DPRNT/POPEN go to an external device. A provenance comment next to `onProbeResult` says so, and output is unchanged.
- **Sinumerik and Heidenhain:** these posts have no probe hooks yet. The decision file records the future choice: Sinumerik `MSG("PROBE X ERROR "<<R190)` then `MSG()`; Heidenhain none until FN16 to `SCREEN:` is confirmed not to stop.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/575-probe-report.md`.

**Golden diffs:** only the Tormach probe goldens changed. Each gains one `(DEBUG, PROBE <axis> ERROR #19n)` line after its `o90n endif`: `probe_face`, `probe_edge`, `probe_corner`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_bore_centre_mm` and `probe_boss_centre`. Fanuc probe goldens and all cutting goldens are byte-identical.

## How tested
- **New `probe_report` (4):**
  - `tormach_face_reports_z_after_its_tolerance_test_and_before_g10`
  - `tormach_corner_reports_each_axis_before_g10`
  - `tormach_measure_only_reports_before_its_stop`
  - `fanuc_has_no_non_stopping_message_so_writes_no_report`
  - The three Tormach tests failed before the change.
- **Gate:** probe_tormach 7, probe_op 12, conformance, posting, tormach_post, fanuc_post, probe_reach, heidenhain_block_form, inverted_post and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
Seeing the DEBUG line on the real control. That can ride with #521's remaining mm run.

Changelog: Probe programs report each probed axis's measured deviation before writing the work offset: Tormach/PathPilot shows (DEBUG, PROBE <axis> ERROR #19n) without stopping; Fanuc-family controls have no non-stopping message and write none (#575)

Fixes #575

title: feat(post): probing hooks for the Tormach PathPilot post (G38.2)
body:
**Replaces #376** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #333** (`issue/257-gcode-comments`, which also edits `tormach.cps`). This diff includes #333's commits until it merges; the #362 work is the last commit (55b7b83).

## What changed
`assets/posts/tormach.cps` gains `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult` in LinuxCNC/PathPilot words, so a Probe op posts on the Tormach mills instead of being refused by name.

**The touch move**
- It is `G38.2`. The control halts with an error when contact never comes, or when the probe is already tripped at the start, so the post writes no no-contact test of its own.
- XY is positioned first, so a probe never starts from an unknown XY.
- `G38.3` plus a `#5070` test was rejected: it hands that safety from the control to our own branch.

**Reading the trip**
- It is read from `#5061`–`#5063`. These are in the coordinate system the G38 ran in, in program units, so they compare directly with the expected values.

**Back-off and tolerance alarm**
- The back-off is incremental (`G91 G1 … G90`).
- A deviation past the tolerance runs `o9nn if [ABS[#19x] GT tol]` / `(MSG, …)` / `M2` / `o9nn endif`, with a unique O-word per test.
- `M2`, not `M0`, so the operator can't resume onto a wrong offset. `(ABORT,…)` is not in the stable LinuxCNC reference.

**Setting the offset**
- `G10 L20 P<n> X[#5420-#190] …`: the current position in the active offset, minus the deviation. It is exact in either unit.
- `G10 L2` from `#5221+20×slot` was rejected: the reference doesn't say which unit the stored offsets use, so a G21 program on an inch-configured control could mix units.
- With no offset to set, it writes `(MSG, CHECK PROBE RESULT …)` then `M0`.

**Preamble**
- A section at 0 rpm (a touch probe) writes no spindle start, no belt note and no coolant.

**Arming**
- Nothing is written. PathPilot's probe input is always live, and the probe type is a Settings-tab choice.

The sources for every word are in `docs/decisions/362-tormach-probe.md`: the LinuxCNC G-code reference, overview and o-code pages, and Tormach's PathPilot post-processor guidelines and G38.x pages. No other CAM system's output was read.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_tormach.rs` (7 tests). Goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/` on the 770MX (inch): `probe_face`, `probe_edge`, `probe_corner`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_boss_centre`, plus metric `probe_bore_centre_mm`.
- `probe_op::the_tormach_post_probes_the_op_with_g38_2`: the op now posts on Tormach, where it used to be refused.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (macOS): post and app suites all green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean.

## Real-control results (contributor's Tormach 770MX, PathPilot v2.14.4, 2026-11-09)
Recorded in this PR's comments. Every item of the maintainer's hold has now run on a real control:
- **Offset write, inch (twice):** `G10 L20 P1 Z[#5422-#190]` wrote G54 Z. The result agreed with a manual PathPilot touch to 0.0002 in, and two consecutive runs agreed to 0.0003 in.
- **Offset write, mm:** `PROBE Z ERROR -0.002438` mm. An inch re-check right after read 0.000102 in, so the two units agree to under 0.003 mm.
- **Back-off after a trip:** `G91 G1 Z+` retracted away from the face with no "probe tripped during non-probe move" error, and `G90` was restored. The following absolute moves ran as expected.
- **`o9nn if`/`endif`:** accepted, and both runs completed to the last line. The within-tolerance branch was taken, so the out-of-tolerance `(MSG, …)`/`M2` path was not triggered on the machine.

Still not exercised on a real control:
- PathPilot preview behaviour at `M2`;
- `G10 L20 P2` (G55);
- a trip during a positioning move. Since main's #174/#500, positioning is a protected `G38.3` with its own guard, which postdates the real runs.
- `G38.2` with no contact.

Changelog: The Tormach PathPilot post writes the Probe operation (G38.2 touch, tolerance alarm, G10 L20 work offset) instead of refusing it (#362)

Fixes #362
